metas.name: A2 Road Quality
metas.note: • The section of the A2 between Maseru and Mafeteng has by far the best road quality in all of Lesotho.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/lesotho.

metas.name: A25 Katse Reservoir
metas.note:
• There are two large man-made water reservoirs in the mountainous part of Lesotho, which can be seen from several road sections.
  • The larger Katse reservoir is visible from parts of the A25.

NOTE:

  • Do not confuse these with the small industrial lake found near the Letseng diamond mine.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/lesotho.

metas.name: A25 Raindrops
metas.note: • On a section of the A25, just east of the big reservoir, the camera is covered in raindrops in one direction.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/lesotho.

metas.name: A3 Off-Road Mohale Reservoir
metas.note:
• There are two large man-made water reservoirs in the mountainous part of Lesotho, which can be seen from several road sections.
  • The smaller Mohale reservoir is visible from an off-road of the A3.

NOTE:

  • Do not confuse these with the small industrial lake found near the Letseng diamond mine.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/lesotho.

metas.name: A5 Tempoary Bollard
metas.note:
• Several sections of the A5 south of Nyakosoba are under construction.
  • As a result, you will often see a sort of temporary “bollard” next to the road, consisting of a stick that is mostly painted white.
  • Even on sections without the bollard, you can often recognize this road, as it is a wide dirt road with very dark brown soil.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/lesotho.

metas.name: Flat Region
metas.note:
Lesotho Flat Region:

  • In the flat region, the road itself runs through a mostly flat or hilly landscape.
  • “Flat” is a bit of a misnomer, as you will usually still see tabletop-like mountains around you.
  • However they will usually be significantly further away from the road, giving you a more clear line of sight.
  • This “flat” part is the region with the most coverage, settlements and agriculture.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/lesotho.

metas.name: Maseru
metas.note:
• The only city with a significantly urbanised downtown area is Maseru, the capital.
  • All other towns have a very provincial feel in comparison to Maseru.

NOTE:

  • The suburbs of Maseru can still have a very rural feel.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/lesotho.

metas.name: Mountainous Region
metas.note:
Lesotho Mountainous Region:

  • In the mountainous part, the road will usually be directly on the side of the mountain, instead of slightly away from it.
  • The mountains are often large, closer to the road, and covered in green grass.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/lesotho.

metas.name: Qacha's Nek
metas.note:
• Qacha's Nek is a very recognizable town that is located far away from most other towns, on the southeastern border with South Africa.
  • It is situated right in the middle of green mountains, and it had noticeably bad weather when the Google car drove there.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/lesotho.

metas.name: Ramatsediso Road
metas.note:
The road going from Ramatsediso to Sehlabathebe NP, in the southeast on the border with South Africa, is very recognizable.

➖➖➖➖➖

Consider guessing there if the following three things are all true for your location:

  • Unpaved road with light brown soil.
  • Good weather with little fluffy clouds.
  • Grassy landscape high in the mountains.

You will also often be able to see exposed, light-coloured rocks next to the road.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/lesotho.
